correctness.rationale: Passes as repaired in repairs/1/RESULT.md, not on the frozen distinctness argument. Frozen line 44 incorrectly rules out distinct reciprocal D-parameters when lambda^2 is not 1. At lambda=i, p=(1,1,1), eta=i and eta^(-1)=-i are both eligible and both have fixed trace zero, but give the distinct lines x_l=x_k and x_l=-x_k. In general the extra case is lambda^2=-1. The reciprocal slices then have opposite remaining power products epsilon=+1,-1. Each satisfies T_{p_k}(x_k)=epsilon*T_{p_l}(x_l), so their images differ because the Chebyshev trace of the varying coordinate is nonconstant. This closes the proof without narrowing the phase range or changing the count. The finite morphism comes from monic equations for the u_i; the inversion subsets describe its fibers and give generic degree one off lambda=±1. Pairwise coprimality makes each candidate slice an irreducible torus translate. All noninjective fibers and all rank drops have image on the listed curves. A finite singleton immersion is smooth on the image; general points of each curve have two immersed preimages with nonproportional normals, hence a reduced transverse double germ. At lambda=±1 the generic orbit has two points, so the normal quotient is the normalization. Exactly four sign triples satisfy the torus equation, and the local inversion is minus identity on two coordinates, producing four A1 singularities on that quotient. The supplied checker and notes were inspected, not executed; the nine-curve test at lambda=2 does not address reciprocal D-parameters.
residual_risks: The proof concerns reduced affine loci and the generic local type; the repaired result still does not classify exceptional points on the image or give a special-phase census of that image.
